components.calibrationNotes: NOT USABLE AS-IS, two separate real problems found: (1) value mismatch — this resistor's bands are yellow-violet-red-gold = 4700 ohm, not the 220 ohm (red-red-brown-gold) the pilot needed; stock photography can't be commissioned to show an exact value on demand. (2) background-removal failure — the original photo has a wire-stripper tool in sharp focus in the foreground and the resistor slightly out-of-focus behind it; rembg's saliency model kept the sharp tool and erased most of the actual resistor, including its color bands. Confirms the pipeline's search/download/license/manifest steps work correctly; does NOT confirm rembg is reliable on multi-object, multi-depth-of-field stock photos without a manual crop step first.

components.searchQuery: breadboard electronics / empty breadboard no wires / breadboard prototyping board flat lay
components.reason: No candidate met the bar after 3 query variations and reviewing ~8 real photos. Best available were either (a) an empty breadboard still in shrink-wrap packaging on a yellow background, shot at an angle, with plastic glare partly obscuring the hole grid (Pexels photo 35673092), or (b) a genuinely clean top-down empty breadboard with a fully populated circuit on top — components/wires plugged into most holes (Pexels photo 32894960). Neither is an unobstructed, flat, empty grid suitable for pixel-accurate hole calibration. Not selected rather than forcing a poor match.

components.searchQuery: red LED diode component / red LED light close up / 5mm LED bulb electronic component macro / small LED light emitting diode
components.reason: No candidate found across 4 query variations. Pexels' free library returned car tail lights, neon signs, traffic lights, and household screw-base light bulbs for every LED-related query, but no macro photo of an actual 5mm through-hole LED (the small two-legged component this app's breadboard needs). This looks like a real coverage gap in this specific stock library for this specific niche electronic part, not a search-tuning problem.
